nodes.content: Design a multipath transport that preserves reliable ordered delivery, bounded buffering, and bottleneck fairness during asymmetric path failures.
requirements: Maintain delivery progress within 8 MiB receiver buffering whenever at least one path remains usable.
Keep competing single-path flows’ throughput within 10% of their equal-share baseline at shared bottlenecks.

nodes.content: Use DSN-based 8 MiB receive credits, gap-priority retransmission on healthy paths, and shared-bottleneck detection with aggregate TCP-fair congestion control.
How can the sender retransmit a failed path’s missing DSN after out-of-order data exhausts the 8 MiB receive window?
A 64 KiB gap reserve and 16 KiB maximum segment permit missing-DSN retransmissions after out-of-order credits close.
Run ns-3 path-failure sweeps with saturated out-of-order credits, a 64 KiB gap reserve, and 16 KiB segments; measure delivery stalls.
In 1,000 ns-3 failures with saturated out-of-order credits, ordered delivery resumed within 420 ms; peak occupancy was ≤8 MiB.
Adopt the 64 KiB gap reserve and 16 KiB segments: ns-3 showed recovery within 420 ms and ≤8 MiB occupancy.
Implement the adopted gap reserve and 16 KiB segments; test delivery within 8 MiB and ≤10% TCP equal-share loss.
Implement receiver credit accounting with a 64 KiB gap reserve, 16 KiB segment cap, and DSN-priority retransmission queue.
GapCredit v0.1 adds DSN receive-credit accounting, the 64 KiB gap reserve, 16 KiB segment cap, and gap-priority retransmission queue.
Run GapCredit v0.1 failover and shared-bottleneck TCP coexistence tests, measuring peak occupancy, recovery time, and equal-share deviation.
In GapCredit v0.1 tests, failover resumed within 410 ms at ≤8 MiB; competing TCP retained ≥95% equal-share throughput.
Gap-repair permits plus highest-DSN eviction restore delivery with an exhausted 8 MiB receive window, without reserving credit.
In ns-3, test reserve-free gap-repair permits with highest-DSN eviction under saturated 8 MiB windows; measure recovery and occupancy.
In 1,000 ns-3 failures, 42 reserve-free runs stalled >10 s despite a usable path as eviction churn delayed gap repairs.
How quickly must shared-bottleneck detection couple congestion windows after asymmetric degradation to preserve competing TCP’s ≥90% equal-share throughput?
Sweep shared-bottleneck detection delays of 1–8 RTTs under asymmetric path loss in ns-3; measure competing TCP equal-share throughput.
Under asymmetric loss, shared-queue detection misclassified at every 1–8-RTT setting; competing TCP retained only 84–88% equal-share throughput.
Use one TCP-equivalent aggregate AIMD window across all paths, retaining the 64 KiB gap reserve and gap-priority retransmissions.
Replace detection with always-coupled aggregate AIMD, then sweep asymmetric loss and verify competing TCP stays ≥90% of equal share.
Integrate always-coupled aggregate AIMD into GapCredit v0.1, sharing one congestion window across paths while preserving gap-priority retransmission.
GapCredit v0.2 replaces shared-bottleneck detection with one aggregate AIMD window while retaining v0.1 receive credits and gap repair.
Run GapCredit v0.2 ns-3 asymmetric-loss sweeps against single-path TCP; measure equal-share retention, recovery time, and peak receive occupancy.
Across 1,000 asymmetric-loss ns-3 runs, GapCredit v0.2 kept TCP throughput ≥94% of equal share, recovery ≤450 ms, occupancy ≤8 MiB.
Adopt always-coupled AIMD: TCP retained ≥94% equal share versus detection’s 84–88%, with ≤450 ms recovery and ≤8 MiB occupancy.
Benchmark GapCredit v0.1 versus v0.2 under asymmetric failures and shared bottlenecks, comparing TCP equal-share retention, delivery stalls, and peak buffering.
Under asymmetric failures, v0.1 left TCP at 86% equal share; v0.2 retained 95%, with zero stalls and ≤8 MiB buffering.
Quarantining a blackholed path after two RTOs prevents repeated aggregate-window collapse while retaining ≥90% TCP equal-share throughput.
When should a blackholed path be quarantined to avoid repeated aggregate-window collapse without reducing competing TCP below 90% equal share?
Sweep 1-, 2-, and 4-RTO quarantine thresholds in ns-3 blackhole tests; measure aggregate-window collapses and competing TCP equal-share retention.
At two RTOs, 18% of blackhole runs suffered ≥2 aggregate-window collapses despite competing TCP retaining 94% equal share.
First-RTO quarantine with one-segment probes every four RTTs reduces repeated window collapses below 1% while TCP retains ≥90% equal share.
Run 1,000 ns-3 blackhole trials with first-RTO quarantine and four-RTT probes; measure repeated collapses and TCP equal-share retention.
In 1,000 blackhole trials, first-RTO quarantine yielded 0.7% repeated collapses; competing TCP retained 93% equal-share throughput.
Extend GapCredit v0.2 with first-RTO path quarantine, four-RTT one-segment recovery probes, and gap-priority retransmission under aggregate AIMD.
How many successful recovery probes should release a quarantined path without triggering another aggregate-window collapse?
Two consecutive ACKed probes before reactivation, followed by a one-MSS-per-RTT path ramp, keep repeated collapses below 1%.
Use e8’s 0.7% collapse rate as control; compare two-ACK, one-MSS/RTT reactivation under reserved-credit and reserve-free gap-permit highest-DSN eviction.
In 1,000 two-ACK reactivation trials, reserve-free gap permits yielded zero >10 s stalls, ≤8 MiB occupancy, and 0.8% repeated collapses.
Use e8’s 0.7% baseline and e9’s two-ACK configuration in repeated-blackhole trials; measure window collapses and TCP equal-share retention.
In 1,000 repeated-blackhole trials, two-ACK reactivation caused 6.2% repeated collapses; competing TCP retained 92% equal share.
Require three consecutive ACKed probes and one loss-free RTO before one-MSS/RTT reactivation; predict <1% repeated collapses under recurring blackholes.
Use e8 and e10 controls to benchmark three-ACK plus loss-free-RTO reactivation across 1,000 recurring-blackhole ns-3 trials.
In 1,000 recurring-blackhole trials, three-ACK plus loss-free-RTO reactivation caused 2.3% repeated collapses, exceeding the predicted <1%.
Benchmark three-ACK, loss-free-RTO reactivation on bursty-blackhole traces against e8’s 0.7% and e10’s 6.2% repeated-collapse baselines.
On bursty-blackhole traces, three-ACK reactivation produced 0.8% repeated collapses, below 1% and e10’s 6.2% two-ACK baseline.
Run paired mixed-blackhole trials comparing two-ACK and three-ACK-plus-loss-free-RTO reactivation against e8/e10 controls; measure repeated collapses and TCP fairness.
Across 1,000 mixed-blackhole trials, two-ACK reactivation yielded 0.9% repeated collapses; competing TCP retained 93% equal-share throughput.
Across 1,000 mixed-blackhole trials, three-ACK reactivation caused 1.7% repeated collapses, exceeding h6’s <1% prediction.
Extend GapCredit v0.2 with first-RTO quarantine, a 64 KiB gap reserve, and exponential cooldown after failed two-ACK reactivations.
Which cooldown base and cap keep repeated collapses below 1% during recurring blackholes while preserving TCP’s ≥90% equal share?
An exponential cooldown starting at four RTTs and capped at 64 RTTs keeps recurring-blackhole collapses below 1%.
Against e11–e14 baselines, sweep cooldown bases of 2/4/8 RTTs and caps of 32/64/128 RTTs; measure collapses and TCP fairness.
In 1,000 recurring-blackhole trials, 4–64-RTT cooldown yielded 0.6% repeated collapses; competing TCP retained 93% equal-share throughput.
Implement first-RTO quarantine and e15’s 4–64-RTT cooldown in GapCredit; verify progress within 8 MiB and TCP ≥90% equal-share.
Implement first-RTO quarantine, two-ACK reactivation, and 4–64-RTT exponential cooldown in GapCredit v0.2’s path scheduler.
GapCredit v0.3 adds first-RTO path quarantine, two-ACK reactivation, and 4–64-RTT exponential cooldown to the v0.2 scheduler.
Test GapCredit v0.3 in ns-3 asymmetric failures and recurring blackholes; measure delivery stalls, peak buffering, collapses, and TCP equal-share retention.
In 1,000 ns-3 trials, v0.3 had zero delivery stalls, ≤8 MiB occupancy, 0.7% repeated collapses, and ≥93% TCP equal-share throughput.
Adopt GapCredit v0.3: 1,000 trials showed no delivery stalls, ≤8 MiB buffering, and competing TCP ≥93% equal share.
